title: NEB Class 11 Chemistry — Stoichiometry — 2024
subject: chemistry
source: NEB Grade 11 Model Questions / NEB Past Papers 2020-2024

questions.question: What is the mole concept? Calculate the number of molecules in 36 g of water.
questions.solution:
**Mole:** the amount containing as many particles as atoms in exactly 12 g of carbon-12 — one mole = 6.022 × 10²³ particles.

Moles of H₂O = 36/18 = 2 mol. Molecules = 2 × 6.022 × 10²³ = **1.204 × 10²⁴**.
questions.knowledgeNote: M(H₂O) = 18 g/mol; at STP, 1 mol of any gas occupies 22.4 L.

questions.question: Calculate the empirical formula of a compound containing 40% carbon, 6.67% hydrogen, and 53.33% oxygen by mass.
questions.solution:
Per 100 g: C = 40/12 = 3.33 mol; H = 6.67/1 = 6.67 mol; O = 53.33/16 = 3.33 mol.

Divide by 3.33: C:H:O = 1:2:1 → empirical formula **CH₂O**.
questions.knowledgeNote: Percent → mass (per 100 g) → moles (÷ atomic mass) → simplest ratio — the fixed four-step ritual.

questions.question: 10 g of H₂ reacts with 64 g of O₂ to form water. Which is the limiting reagent, and what is the maximum mass of water formed?
questions.solution:
2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O. Moles: H₂ = 10/2 = 5 mol; O₂ = 64/32 = 2 mol.

2 mol O₂ needs 4 mol H₂ (5 available) — **O₂ is limiting**.

Water formed = 4 mol × 18 = **72 g**.
questions.knowledgeNote: Limiting reagent = the reactant exhausted first — always compare mole ratios, never gram amounts.

questions.question: 4 g of NaOH is dissolved in water to make 250 mL of solution. Calculate its molarity. (NaOH = 40)
questions.knowledgeNote: Molarity is moles per LITRE of solution — convert mL to L before dividing.

questions.question: A compound has empirical formula CH₂O and molar mass 180 g/mol. Find its molecular formula.
questions.solution:
Empirical mass = 12 + 2 + 16 = 30. n = 180/30 = 6.

Molecular formula = 6 × CH₂O = **C₆H₁₂O₆** (glucose).
questions.knowledgeNote: Molecular = n × empirical, where n = molar mass / empirical mass — always an integer.

questions.question: In an experiment, the theoretical yield is 50 g but only 40 g of product is obtained. Calculate the percentage yield.
questions.solution:
% yield = (actual/theoretical) × 100 = (40/50) × 100 = **80%**.

Losses come from side reactions, incomplete reaction, and handling/spillage.
questions.knowledgeNote: % yield never exceeds 100 — an answer above it means the product is wet or impure.
